Sexton, 102 ft. 2½ ins.; 4th, Marshall, 87 ft. 1¾ ins. Weight: 3rd, Law, 33 ft. 5½ ins.; 4th, Morrison, 28 ft. 3½ ins. Result: L.A.C., 34 points; Belgrave, 40 points.
In the 440 yards Morrison was second in a 54.3 heat but failed to get placed in a 51.8 final. Hazell our only representative in the mile failed to survive.

Match Events: 100 yards: 1, Marshall, 10.9 secs.; 3rd, Rae. 220 yards: Picton (W. and B.), 25 secs.; 2nd, Law (B); 3rd, Marsh (B). 440 yards: Morrison (B), 54.7 secs.; 3rd, Tranter (B). 880 yards: 1st, Tranter (B); Chitty (B). 1 mile: 2nd, Hazel.

Marshall and Mullen also competed and were each placed fourth in their heats both clocking 23.7 secs. Morrison was fourth in his 440 yards heat in 55 secs. In the mile walk Roast was third and Shepherd fourth.
In the junior match Paddy Mullen was second in the 100 yards and Dave Marshall second in the 220. Tapley and Morrison were second and third in the quarter and Tranter second in the 880.
Morrison of Dartford and Ellam of Rochester were sharing a lead of 75 yds. Ellam eventually pulled away to win by eighteen seconds in a new course record time of 26.12.
With Hampshire and Morrison making their first appearances of the season, and packing well in with David Cocks, Belgrave swept the board in the Boys event.
Hampshire wasted no time on the third leg disposing of this solitary escapee and then proceeded to open up an invaluable gap, the size of which must have been most comforting to young Morrison.
Hampshire, Morrison, Hudson and Williams were 1st, 2nd, 4th and 7th in the Aristotle School Championships.

…b 7-21 Jack himself recorded the same time on the next leg-taking us up two further places, and 7 minutes-41 secs later Morrison crossed the finishing line in fourth place to set the seal on a fine team performance. 135 runners took part and Redwood and Hampshire were 9th fastest of the day.…

We were then only eleven seconds in arrears when Morrison took over for the last leg. Despite a gallant effort Morrison was forced back to third but in finishing only fourteen seconds behind Guildford & Godalming and six behind Mitcham we can consider our team to have performed admirably; especially…
Also competed:- Morrison, Hampshire, Yeo, Startup, Rendle, Finn, Satchell, Sturgess, Crosbie, Pearce, Williams, Dawson.

How encouraging to see Belgrave vests proudly and prominently worn by so many of the runners; and what a testimony to the Club's future that Belgrave boys should win both the races. Well done, Hudson and Morrison!

In a Junior match Mitcham proved too strong for us but all praise to Cocks for his win in the 440 (50.6) and for grand supporting roles played by Redwood (4:35·7) Mead (55.8), Morrison (2:2.1) and Pottinger (19'11½") in their respective events.

New blood is continueing to flow into our membership and there is a good chance that McGrath and Saunders (both Juniors) and Morrison (just a Senior) will blend with our more established walkers and play a leading part in Belgrave's resurgence.
Several promising cadets have come our way but none more interesting than Morrison who, besides being a promising walker, is quite an outstanding golfer.
JOHN BICOURT showed fine early season form at Parliament Hill on October 18th when he finished third behind Morrison and Gunstone in the London Colleges League.
